payload.rationale:
The supplied January–August NASA GISS anomalies average 1.22375°C. The contractual hurdle is an annual reported value above both 1.28°C and 2025’s 1.19°C—not necessarily above 2024’s supplied 1.29°C. With annual reporting rounded to hundredths, a qualifying 1.29°C would require September–December to average approximately 1.408°C, assuming equal monthly weighting and no revisions. Simply repeating August’s 1.40°C would leave the annual average near 1.2825°C, likely reported as 1.28°C and therefore insufficient.

Nevertheless, August was substantially warmer than the preceding months. The supplied September NOAA discussion reports strengthening El Niño and forecasts greater than 90% probability of a very strong fall/winter event. My transfer assumption is that this favors sustained or increasing global warmth, making the required final-four-month average more likely than not. That ENSO probability is not the probability of this contract resolving YES; the global response has variable magnitude and timing.

The strongest reason my 68% estimate could be too high is that August could be a temporary spike and much of the El Niño warming could arrive in 2027. The strongest reason it could be too low is that the unusually strong developing El Niño could sustain anomalies comfortably above 1.41°C throughout the remaining months. This is a judgmental forecast, not a fitted statistical probability.
limitations: Four monthly values and the annual settlement value remain unknown.
No fitted ENSO-to-GISS forecasting model or calibrated residual distribution is supplied.
Monthly and annual data can be revised; rounding matters near the contractual threshold.
Source captures are partial and cannot be independently verified without browsing.
